findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Containers of turkey, roast beef, and cheese did not have date marks. One container had a day dot of Thursday, but no date was written on the label. Containers of salami and pepperoni had date marks of 5/22. Both packaged keep refrigerated. Salami and pepperoni were discarded in the trash. Benefit of doubt was given for turkey, roast beef, and cheese - items were dated and kept for use.

Refrigerated potentially hazardous food must be properly dated and used or discarded within 7 days. Day 1 starts as soon as the original packaging is opened. For example, salami opened today would need to be dated 6/2 and used or discarded by the end of operations next Monday (6/8). Freezing foods will stop the 7 day clock but does not reset it. Time frame for use once a product is pulled from the freezer and thawed is dependent upon when the food was frozen. If frozen the same day of opening, then once thawed it must be used or discarded w/in 6 days. If frozen on day 4 then once thawed it would have a use by or discard time frame of 3 days. Keep track of dates on all foods. Make sure frozen portions of foods are properly dated as to when they are pulled from the freezer and thawed for use to avoid confusion on the proper use by/discard time frame.

Use soap/running water, wash for 20 seconds, dry hands with clean paper towels, and use paper towels as barrier to turn off faucet when done.
Wash hands before putting on gloves and between glove changes. Gloves are meant for only one task and must be discarded when soiled (touch any surface not related to food/clean equipment), torn, or an interruption in task occurs.
